system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided simdjson codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Your task is to analyze the simdjson codebase on branch branch-02. Identify the specific regressions introduced in DOM streaming, element access, and ondemand parser configuration. Write your findings to /tmp/outputs/review.md

rubric.criterion: Identifies the spurious wakeup race in include/simdjson/dom/document_stream-inl.h in stage1_worker::finish where cond_var.wait(lock) is used without a predicate, allowing stage2 to proceed before stage1 completes

Identifies the source slice bug in include/simdjson/dom/document_stream-inl.h in iterator::source where object_or_array uses next_structural_index instead of next_structural_index - 1, causing the returned view to include the first byte of the next document

Identifies the pointer unescape inconsistency in include/simdjson/dom/element-inl.h in element::at_pointer where pointer segments are unescaped before dispatch, creating inconsistent behavior with object and array at_pointer and failing for escaped keys

Identifies the cross-document ordering bug in include/simdjson/dom/element-inl.h in element::operator< where ordering is derived from pointer arithmetic of doc pointers, leading to unstable or meaningless ordering across documents

Identifies the case-insensitive lookup regression in include/simdjson/dom/object-inl.h in object::at_key_case_insensitive where key_equals is used instead of key_equals_case_insensitive, breaking mixed-case lookups
Identifies the array size accounting bug in include/simdjson/dom/array-inl.h in array::size where number_of_slots is returned instead of scope_count, inflating size for nested arrays or objects

Identifies the shared parser race in include/simdjson/generic/ondemand/parser-inl.h in parser::get_threadlocal_parser_if_exists where a static parser is used instead of thread_local, causing cross-thread data races and buffer corruption

Identifies the inverted clamp bug in include/simdjson/generic/ondemand/parser-inl.h in parser::set_max_capacity where large values are clamped down to MINIMAL_DOCUMENT_CAPACITY and small values are accepted, leading to unexpected CAPACITY errors
